notes.definition: Condensation polymerisation (Higher tier) involves monomers that each have two functional groups. When the monomers react they join together and usually lose a small molecule such as water each time a link forms, so the reactions are called condensation reactions.
explanation: In condensation polymerisation each monomer has two functional groups, one at each end. A functional group on one monomer reacts with a functional group on the next monomer, forming a link between them. Each time a link forms, a small molecule, usually water, is released. Because a small molecule is lost, the reaction is called a condensation reaction. Since each monomer has a reactive group at both ends, the chain can keep growing in both directions to form a polymer.

The simplest condensation polymers are made from two different monomers, each with two of the same functional group. For example, a diol (a molecule with two –OH groups), such as ethane diol HO–CH₂–CH₂–OH, can react with a dicarboxylic acid (a molecule with two –COOH groups), such as hexanedioic acid HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH. The –COOH group of the acid reacts with the –OH group of the alcohol to form an ester link (–COO–) and water, just like making ethyl ethanoate. Because the polymer contains many ester links, it is called a polyester.

We often show the monomers using blocks to stand for the carbon chain in the middle, since only the functional groups take part. The diol is HO–□–OH and the dicarboxylic acid is HOOC–○–COOH. For n of each monomer, the equation is: n HO–□–OH + n HOOC–○–COOH → –[O–□–O–OC–○–CO]ₙ– + 2n H₂O. Two water molecules are released for each repeating unit, because each unit contains two ester links, one at each end.

Condensation polymerisation is different from addition polymerisation. Addition polymers are made from one type of monomer with a C=C double bond, and the polymer is the only product, so the repeating unit has the same atoms as the monomer. Condensation polymers are usually made from two different monomers, each with two functional groups, and a small molecule such as water is produced as well as the polymer. So the repeating unit has fewer atoms than the monomers added together: H₂O is missing for each link.

To work out the repeating unit from the monomers, remove an H from the –OH end of the diol and an –OH from each –COOH end of the acid, then join the remaining parts. To work out the monomers from a polyester, split each ester link (–COO–) between the C=O carbon and the oxygen, and add –OH to the C=O carbon and H to the oxygen. Polyesters are used to make fibres for clothing and plastic drinks bottles (PET).
keyFacts: Condensation polymerisation uses monomers with two functional groups each.
When the monomers join, a small molecule (usually water) is lost each time.
Simplest example: a diol + a dicarboxylic acid → a polyester + water.
Ethane diol (HO–CH₂–CH₂–OH) + hexanedioic acid (HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH) → polyester + water.
The –OH and –COOH groups react to form an ester link, –COO–.
Addition polymers: one monomer with C=C, one product only.
Condensation polymers: usually two monomers, two products (polymer + small molecule).
The repeating unit has fewer atoms than the monomers combined.

keyTerms.definition: Polymerisation in which monomers with two functional groups join, releasing a small molecule such as water each time a link forms.
A reaction in which two molecules join together and a small molecule, such as water, is lost.
A molecule with two –OH (alcohol) functional groups, such as ethane diol.
A molecule with two –COOH functional groups, such as hexanedioic acid.
A condensation polymer whose monomers are joined by ester links (–COO–).
The –COO– group formed when a –COOH group reacts with an –OH group.
The part of a polymer that repeats along the chain, shown in brackets with n.

equations.name: Making a polyester (block form)
equations.formula: n diol + n dicarboxylic acid → polyester + 2n water

workedExamples.title: Counting water molecules
workedExamples.question: A polyester molecule is made from 300 molecules of a diol and 300 molecules of a dicarboxylic acid. How many water molecules are released?
steps: Each repeating unit contains one diol and one acid, so n = 300.
The equation shows 2n H₂O are released.

workedExamples.title: Mr of the repeating unit
workedExamples.question: Ethane diol (Mr 62) and hexanedioic acid (Mr 146) form a polyester. Calculate the Mr of the repeating unit. (Mr of H₂O = 18)
steps: One repeating unit is made from one diol and one acid: 62 + 146 = 208.
Two water molecules are lost per unit: 2 × 18 = 36.

workedExamples.title: Identifying monomers from a polyester
workedExamples.question: A polyester has the repeating unit –[O–□–O–OC–○–CO]–. Give the monomers in block form.
steps: Split each ester link between the C=O carbon and the O.
Add H to each O end: HO–□–OH (a diol).
Add OH to each C=O end: HOOC–○–COOH (a dicarboxylic acid).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think condensation polymerisation needs a C=C double bond, like addition polymerisation.
misconceptions.right: In fact it needs two functional groups on each monomer (such as –OH or –COOH); no double bond is needed.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often say only one water molecule is released per repeating unit.
misconceptions.right: In fact each repeating unit of a polyester contains two ester links, so 2n H₂O are released for n repeating units.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the repeating unit of a condensation polymer has the same atoms as the monomers.
misconceptions.right: In fact atoms are lost as water, so the repeating unit has fewer atoms than the two monomers added together.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think 'condensation' means a gas turning into a liquid here.
misconceptions.right: In fact in chemistry a condensation reaction is one in which two molecules join and a small molecule is lost.

realWorld: Polyester fibres are spun into fabrics for clothing, bedding and sails.
PET, a polyester, is used to make plastic drinks bottles and can be recycled into fleece fabric.
Some polyesters are biodegradable and used for dissolvable stitches.
higherTier: All of this subtopic is Higher tier only (and separate Chemistry only): monomers with two functional groups, loss of small molecules, diol + dicarboxylic acid → polyester + water, and representing monomers and repeating units with blocks.
separateOnlyContent: Condensation polymerisation is only in separate Chemistry (8462), not Combined Science.
examTips: You do not need to remember complex structures: use blocks for the carbon chain and show only the functional groups.
Always state the small molecule lost (usually water) and that each monomer has two functional groups.
In the equation, balance water as 2n H₂O for a diol and dicarboxylic acid.
For comparison questions, compare monomers, functional groups and number of products for both types.
summary: Condensation polymers form from monomers with two functional groups.
A small molecule, usually water, is lost each time monomers join.
Ester links (–COO–) join the monomers in a polyester.
Addition: one product. Condensation: polymer + small molecule.
Use blocks to represent the monomers.

questions.question: Which small molecule is usually released during condensation polymerisation?
questions.explanation: When –OH and –COOH groups react, an H and an OH are removed as H₂O.

questions.question: How many functional groups does each monomer in condensation polymerisation have?
questions.explanation: Two functional groups, one at each end, let the chain grow in both directions.

questions.question: What type of polymer is made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: –OH and –COOH groups react to form ester links, so the polymer is a polyester.

questions.question: Which functional groups are found in ethane diol?
questions.explanation: 'Diol' means two alcohol (–OH) groups: HO–CH₂–CH₂–OH.

questions.question: Which link is formed when a –COOH group reacts with an –OH group?
questions.explanation: This is the same reaction as making an ester such as ethyl ethanoate.

questions.question: Which is a difference between addition and condensation polymerisation?
options: Only addition polymerisation forms long chains
Condensation polymerisation also produces a small molecule such as water
markScheme: 1 mark: condensation also produces a small molecule
questions.explanation: Addition gives only the polymer; condensation gives the polymer and a small molecule.

questions.question: In the equation n HO–□–OH + n HOOC–○–COOH → polyester + x H₂O, what is x?
questions.explanation: Each repeating unit has two ester links, each releasing one water molecule, so 2n H₂O.

questions.question: Which repeating unit is formed from HO–□–OH and HOOC–○–COOH?
questions.explanation: Remove H from each –OH of the diol and OH from each –COOH of the acid, then join the parts with ester links.

questions.question: Which pair of monomers could form a condensation polymer?
markScheme: 1 mark: ethane diol and hexanedioic acid
questions.explanation: Each has two functional groups, so chains can grow. Ethanol and ethanoic acid have only one group each, so they form a single ester molecule, not a polymer.

questions.question: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ethane diol, HOCH₂CH₂OH (C₂H₆O₂). (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Carbon: 2 × 12 = 24; hydrogen: 6 × 1 = 6; oxygen: 2 × 16 = 32. Total 24 + 6 + 32 = 62.

questions.question: A polyester is made from 500 diol molecules and 500 dicarboxylic acid molecules. Use the equation n HO–□–OH + n HOOC–○–COOH → polyester + 2n H₂O to calculate the number of water molecules released.
questions.explanation: n = 500 and the equation releases 2n H₂O, so 2 × 500 = 1000 water molecules.

questions.question: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of hexanedioic acid, HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH (C₆H₁₀O₄). (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
Ethane diol (Mr = 62) reacts with hexanedioic acid (Mr = 146) to form a polyester. Calculate the Mr of one repeating unit. (Mr of H₂O = 18)
questions.explanation: Two water molecules are lost for each repeating unit, so subtract 36.

questions.question: 62 g of ethane diol reacts completely with 146 g of hexanedioic acid, releasing 36 g of water. Calculate the mass of polyester formed.
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved: total mass of reactants = mass of polyester + mass of water.

questions.question: State why this type of polymerisation is called 'condensation'.
markScheme: 1 mark: a small molecule (such as water) is lost when the monomers join
questions.explanation: A condensation reaction joins two molecules with the loss of a small molecule.

questions.question: Name the two products formed when ethane diol reacts with hexanedioic acid.
questions.explanation: Ester links form between the monomers and water is released.

questions.question: Explain why ethanol and ethanoic acid react to form a single ester molecule, but ethane diol and hexanedioic acid form a polymer.
markScheme: 1 mark: ethanol and ethanoic acid each have only one functional group, so the reaction stops after one link
1 mark: ethane diol and hexanedioic acid each have two functional groups, so links form at both ends and the chain keeps growing
questions.explanation: Two reactive ends on every monomer allow a chain to build up.

questions.question: Using blocks to represent the carbon chains, write the general formulae of a diol and a dicarboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Only the functional groups react, so the rest of the molecule can be shown as a block.

questions.question: Explain why the repeating unit of a polyester does not have the same atoms as the two monomers added together.
markScheme: 1 mark: water (small molecules) is lost when the links form
1 mark: so H and OH atoms (2 H₂O per unit) are missing from the repeating unit
questions.explanation: Unlike addition polymerisation, some atoms leave as water.

questions.question: Write the equation, using blocks, for the formation of a polyester from n molecules of HO–□–OH and n molecules of HOOC–○–COOH.
markScheme: 1 mark: correct repeating unit with brackets and n
questions.explanation: Each repeating unit contains two ester links, so 2n water molecules are formed.

questions.question: A polyester has the repeating unit –[O–CH₂CH₂CH₂–O–OC–C₆H₄–CO]–. Give the formulae of the two monomers.
questions.explanation: Add H to each oxygen end and OH to each C=O end to rebuild the monomers.

questions.question: Suggest why a dicarboxylic acid cannot form an addition polymer on its own.
markScheme: 1 mark: addition polymerisation needs a C=C double bond
1 mark: a dicarboxylic acid (e.g. hexanedioic acid) has no C=C, only –COOH groups
questions.explanation: Its functional groups can only react by condensation with another functional group such as –OH.

questions.question: Describe how a polyester is formed from ethane diol and hexanedioic acid.
markScheme: Indicative content: ethane diol has two –OH groups; hexanedioic acid has two –COOH groups; –OH reacts with –COOH; ester link –COO– forms; water is released each time (condensation); monomers join alternately in a long chain; chain grows at both ends; n HO–□–OH + n HOOC–○–COOH → polyester + 2n H₂O.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear description of the functional groups reacting, ester links and water lost, building a chain.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, e.g. the two monomers join and make water.
questions.explanation: Name the functional groups, the link formed and the small molecule released.

questions.question: Compare addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation. Use poly(ethene) and a polyester as examples, and refer to the monomers, functional groups, products and repeating units.
markScheme: Indicative content: addition: monomer is an alkene (ethene) with a C=C double bond; usually one type of monomer; C=C opens and monomers join; only one product; repeating unit has the same atoms as the monomer, e.g. –[CH₂–CH₂]ₙ–; condensation: monomers have two functional groups (e.g. diol with two –OH and dicarboxylic acid with two –COOH); usually two different monomers; ester links form; a small molecule (water) is lost each time; two products: polyester and water (2n H₂O); repeating unit has fewer atoms than the monomers combined, e.g. –[O–□–O–OC–○–CO]ₙ–.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed comparison covering monomers, functional groups, products and repeating units for both types, with correct examples.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): several valid comparisons with some reference to examples.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two simple differences.
questions.explanation: A good comparison pairs each feature: 'addition gives one product, whereas condensation also gives water'.

questions.question: Hexanedioic acid is a dicarboxylic acid. How many –COOH groups does it have?
questions.explanation: 'Di' means two, so a dicarboxylic acid has two –COOH groups, one at each end.

questions.question: Name the type of link that joins the monomers in a polyester.
questions.explanation: A polyester has many ester links, formed when –COOH reacts with –OH.
